hook.situation: You ask a classmate about a presentation assignment before midterms, plan when to start studying, talk about exam period, and explain why grades or scholarships matter.
objectives: Talk about assignments, presentations, midterms, finals, semesters, grades, and study plans.
Use V아/어야 해요, V기로 했어요, V기 시작하다, N 동안, and V기 위해서 in school-life sentences.
Separate class obligations, personal decisions, study periods, and exam goals.
hook.whyItMatters: Education Korean is deadline-heavy. Learners need more than 학교 and 시험: they need to say what must be finished, what was decided, when exam period lasts, and why they are studying.

grammarNotes.title: V-아/어야 해요 — have to / must
grammarNotes.func: Expresses obligation or necessity: something you have to do. In school life it covers class rules, assignments, deadlines, and things teachers require of students.

formTable.when: Verb stem ends in ㅏ or ㅗ
Verb stem ends in any other vowel

formTable.ex: 내다 → 내야 돼요 (have to hand it in)

examples.en: I have to hand in the homework by tomorrow.
examples.note: 내다 (to hand in) is the core homework verb; -까지 marks the deadline.

examples.en: During class you have to turn off your phone.
examples.note: 끄다 has a ㅡ stem; ㅡ drops before -어야, giving 꺼야 — a common spelling to notice.

examples.ko: 시험이 있어서 오늘 도서관에 가야 해요.
examples.romanization: siheomi isseoseo oneul doseogwane gaya haeyo.
examples.en: I have a test, so I have to go to the library today.
examples.note: 가다 ends in ㅏ, so it takes -아야; 도서관 keeps it in the school setting.

examples.en: In the classroom you have to speak in Korean.
examples.note: 말하다 is a 하다 verb → 해야; a typical classroom rule.

keyPoint.label: -아/어야 해요 vs. -아/어야 돼요
keyPoint.body: Both mean 'have to,' and in everyday speech they are interchangeable. -아/어야 돼요 sounds a touch more colloquial and is very common when talking; -아/어야 해요 is a little more neutral and shows up more in writing. Pick whichever you hear most — the meaning does not change.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 말해야 is pronounced [마래야]: the ㅎ weakens between vowels. 해야 해요 keeps two clear 해 syllables — don't blur them into one.

drill.instruction: Change each verb to the -아/어야 해요 form to state a school obligation.
items: 책을 읽다 → 책을 ___ (have to read the book)
교복을 입다 → 교복을 ___ (have to wear the uniform)
일찍 오다 → 일찍 ___ (have to come early)

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'I need to / it's necessary' tempts learners to add 필요해요. Korean already builds the necessity into -아/어야 해요, so adding 필요하다 on top is redundant and unnatural.

grammarNotes.title: V-기로 했어요 — decided to V
grammarNotes.func: States a decision, plan, or promise that you (or a group) have already made. Common when classmates agree on a study plan or you resolve to do something for school.

formTable.when: Any verb, attach to the plain stem

formTable.ex: 지각 안 하기로 했어요 (decided not to be late)

formTable.when: A standing rule (let's make it a habit)
formTable.ex: 매일 복습하기로 해요 (let's review every day)

examples.en: I decided to study with my friends at the library.
examples.note: A shared decision; 하고 같이 marks who you made the plan with.

examples.en: This semester I decided not to be absent.
examples.note: Negative form uses -지 않기로; 결석하다 (to be absent) ties it to attendance.

examples.en: We decided to study for the test together on the weekend.
examples.note: A mutual promise between classmates — a very typical use.

examples.ko: 선생님이 다음 주에 시험을 보기로 했어요.
examples.romanization: seonsaengnimi daeum jue siheomeul bogiro haesseoyo.
examples.en: The teacher decided to give a test next week.
examples.note: The subject doesn't have to be 'I'; here the teacher made the decision.

keyPoint.label: -기로 했어요 vs. -(으)ㄹ 거예요
keyPoint.body: -기로 했어요 highlights that a decision was made (often jointly or as a resolution). -(으)ㄹ 거예요 just states a future plan or prediction. Use -기로 했어요 when the point is 'we agreed/decided,' not merely 'I will.'

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 했어요 is pronounced [해써요] with a tense ㅆ. 않기로 is read [안키로]: the ㅎ of 않 fuses with the following ㄱ into an aspirated [키].

drill.instruction: Turn each plan into a decision with -기로 했어요.
drill.model: 매일 단어를 외우다 → 매일 단어를 외우기로 했어요.
items: 동아리에 들다 → 동아리에 ___ (decided to join the club)
수업을 빠지지 않다 → 수업을 ___ (decided not to skip class)
도서관에서 만나다 → 도서관에서 ___ (decided to meet at the library)

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners translate 'decided to study' literally with 결정하다 + a nominalized clause. Native speakers package the decision into -기로 하다 instead. Use the idiomatic pattern, not a word-for-word 'decide that.'

grammarNotes.title: V-기 시작하다 — start doing
grammarNotes.func: Says that an action begins or has begun. The verb is nominalized with -기 and followed by 시작하다 (to start). Useful for saying when you started studying, learning, or a new routine.

examples.en: I started learning Korean last year.
examples.note: -부터 marks the starting point in time, pairing naturally with -기 시작하다.

examples.en: After class ended, I started doing my homework.
examples.note: Marks a clear 'began the action' moment right after a school event.

examples.ko: 요즘 시험 때문에 도서관에 다니기 시작했어요.
examples.romanization: yojeum siheom ttaemune doseogwane danigi sijakaesseoyo.
examples.en: These days, because of exams, I've started going to the library.
examples.note: 다니다 (to go regularly) + 시작하다 = the start of a new routine.

examples.en: The teacher started explaining.
examples.note: Any subject works; here the teacher is the one beginning the action.

keyPoint.label: V-기 시작하다 vs. N을/를 시작하다
keyPoint.body: Use V-기 시작하다 to start an action (a verb): 공부하기 시작했어요. To start a thing (a noun), use N을/를 시작하다: 수업을 시작해요 (start the class). Don't say 수업하기 시작하다 when you simply mean 수업을 시작하다.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 시작했어요 is read [시자캐써요]: the ㄱ of 작 + the ㅎ of 했 fuse into an aspirated [ㅋ], and 했어요 becomes [캐써요].

drill.instruction: Combine into one sentence using -기 시작했어요.
items: 아침에 운동 / 하다 → 아침에 운동을 ___ (started exercising in the morning)
책 / 읽다 → 책을 ___ (started reading the book)

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers reach for the heavier -는 것 nominalizer for 'started to learn.' With 시작하다, Korean prefers the lighter -기. -는 것을 시작하다 sounds clumsy and over-literal.

grammarNotes.title: N 동안 — for / during (a period)
grammarNotes.func: Marks a span of time over which something happens: 'for' a duration or 'during' a named period. Essential for saying how long you studied, or that something happened over vacation or a semester.

formTable.ex: 삼 년 동안 (for three years), not 삼 년에 동안

examples.en: I studied at the library for two hours.
examples.note: 두 시간 is a duration, so 동안 means 'for'; no particle between the number phrase and 동안.

examples.en: During vacation I went to a Korean language academy.
examples.note: 방학 (school vacation) is a named period, so 동안 means 'during.'

examples.ko: 시험을 보는 동안 휴대폰을 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.romanization: siheomeul boneun dongan hyudaeponeul sseul su eopseoyo.
examples.en: While taking the test, you can't use your phone.
examples.note: With a verb, use -는 동안 for 'while'; 시험을 보다 (to take a test) sets the school scene.

examples.en: I studied Korean for three years.
examples.note: 삼 년 (three years) is a duration → 'for'; again no particle before 동안.

keyPoint.label: N 동안 (a stretch) vs. N에 (a point)
keyPoint.body: Use 동안 for a span of time you do something over: 세 시간 동안 (for three hours). Use 에 for a single point in time: 세 시에 (at three o'clock). Don't mix them — 세 시간에 or 세 시간에 동안 are both wrong.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 동안 is two even syllables [동안]. 공부했어요 is [공부해써요], with the tense ㅆ in 했.

drill.instruction: Add 동안 (or -는 동안) to express the time span.
drill.model: 한 시간 / 공부하다 → 한 시간 동안 공부했어요.
items: 방학 / 학원에 다니다 → 방학 ___ 학원에 다녔어요
두 시간 / 숙제를 하다 → 두 시간 ___ 숙제를 했어요
수업을 듣다 / 졸다 → 수업을 ___ 졸았어요 (dozed off while in class)

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'for three hours' makes learners insert a particle, but 동안 attaches straight to the time noun with nothing in between. No 에, no 을 before 동안.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-(으)니까 — because / so (reason before a plan)
grammarNotes.func: Gives a reason that leads into a request, suggestion, or plan: 'since A, (let's) B.' In school talk it links why something matters to what you should do next.

examples.en: Grades are important, so let's prepare in advance.
examples.note: Reason (중요하니까) leads into the suggestion.

examples.en: The exam is near, so I study at the library.
examples.note: 가깝다 is ㅂ-irregular: 가까우니까.

examples.en: There's a lot of homework, so let's start today.
examples.note: Consonant stem 많다 → 많으니까.

examples.ko: 수업이 끝났으니까 같이 밥 먹으러 가요.
examples.romanization: sueobi kkeunnasseunikka gachi bap meogeureo gayo.
examples.en: Class is over, so let's go eat together.
examples.note: Past 끝났 + -으니까; reason plus an invitation.

keyPoint.label: -(으)니까 vs. -아/어서 for 'because'
keyPoint.body: Both give reasons, but only -(으)니까 can lead into a command, suggestion, or 'let's' (시험이 가까우니까 공부해요). -아/어서 cannot: you can't say 시험이 가까워서 공부합시다. Use -(으)니까 when the next clause is a request or proposal.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 많으니까 is read [마느니까]: the ㅎ in 많 is silent before a vowel. 끝났으니까 is [끈나쓰니까].

drill.instruction: Join the reason and the plan with -(으)니까.
drill.model: 시험이 가깝다 + 도서관에 가요 → 시험이 가까우니까 도서관에 가요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: When the second clause is a command or suggestion ('take an umbrella'), Korean needs -(으)니까, not -아/어서. -아/어서 only works before a plain statement, not before an order or 'let's.'

grammarNotes.title: V-기 위해서 — in order to (purpose)
grammarNotes.func: Marks a deliberate goal: you do B in order to achieve A. Good for academic goals like passing, getting a scholarship, raising your grade, or getting into a program. Often shortened to -기 위해.

formTable.when: Any verb, attach to the stem
formTable.ex: 합격하다 → 합격하기 위해서 (in order to pass)
받다 → 받기 위해 (in order to get)
늦지 않기 위해서 (in order not to be late)

examples.ko: 좋은 성적을 받기 위해서 매일 공부해요.
examples.romanization: joeun seongjeogeul batgi wihaeseo maeil gongbuhaeyo.
examples.en: I study every day in order to get good grades.
examples.note: 받다 → 받기 위해서; purpose plus the daily habit.

examples.en: I studied hard in order to get a scholarship.
examples.note: Short form -기 위해; a very common academic goal.

examples.en: I go to an academy in order to pass the exam.
examples.note: 합격하다 (to pass) + -기 위해서; 학원 is a private academy.

examples.en: I get up early so as not to be late.
examples.note: Negative goal uses -지 않기 위해서; 지각하다 = to be late to school.

keyPoint.label: V-기 위해서 vs. V-(으)러
keyPoint.body: Both express purpose, but -(으)러 only attaches to motion verbs like 가다/오다 (공부하러 가요 = go to study). -기 위해서 has no such limit and works with any main verb (장학금을 받기 위해서 공부해요). For a goal that isn't 'going somewhere to do it,' use -기 위해서.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 받기 위해서 is read [받끼 위해서]: the ㄷ tenses the following ㄱ to [ㄲ]. 합격하기 is [합껴카기].

drill.model: 좋은 성적을 받다 / 매일 공부해요 → 좋은 성적을 받기 위해서 매일 공부해요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners mix two purpose patterns. Either use -(으)려고 (받으려고 공부해요) OR -기 위해서 (받기 위해서 공부해요), never both together. Don't stack 위해서 after a -(으)려고 ending.

exampleSentence.ko: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: We have to finish the presentation assignment before the midterm.
We decided to finish the assignment before the midterm.

exampleSentence.ko: 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해 매일 공부해야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I have to study every day in order to get a good grade on the final exam.
I reviewed every day during this semester.
I decided to ask the professor.
I have to present in class tomorrow.

exampleSentence.ko: 시험 기간 동안 도서관에서 공부할 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: During exam period, I will study at the library.
I decided to study at the library starting today.

exampleSentence.ko: 장학금을 받기 위해 좋은 성적이 필요해요.
exampleSentence.en: Good grades are necessary in order to get a scholarship.

exampleSentence.ko: 장학금을 받기 위해 좋은 성적이 필요해요.
exampleSentence.en: Good grades are necessary in order to get a scholarship.
I asked the professor a question in order to change my major.
I go to an academy in order to get good at Korean.

extendedDialogue.setting: Classmates plan around a presentation assignment and upcoming exams.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요?
lines.romanization: junggangosa jeone balpyo gwajereul kkeutnaeya haeyo?
lines.en: Do we have to finish the presentation assignment before the midterm?

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 네, 이번 학기 성적에 들어가니까 준비해야 해요.
lines.romanization: ne, ibeon hakgi seongjeoge deureoganikka junbihaeya haeyo.
lines.en: Yes, it counts toward this semester's grade, so we have to prepare.
lines.grammarNote: -니까 gives the reason for the obligation.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그럼 오늘부터 도서관에서 공부하기 시작하기로 했어요.
lines.romanization: geureom oneulbuteo doseogwaneseo gongbuhagi sijakagiro haesseoyo.
lines.en: Then I decided to start studying at the library from today.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해 시험 기간 동안 매일 공부해야 해요.
lines.romanization: gimalgosaeseo joeun seongjeogeul batgi wihae siheom gigan dongan maeil gongbuhaeya haeyo.
lines.en: In order to get a good grade on the final exam, we have to study every day during exam period.
lines.grammarNote: -기 위해 and 동안 explain purpose and duration.

readingText.title: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요
readingText.body: 민서는 이번 학기에 한국어 수업을 듣고 있어요. 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해서 친구와 일정을 정했어요. 발표가 성적에 들어가니까 오늘부터 준비하기 시작하기로 했어요. 시험 기간 동안은 도서관에서 매일 공부할 거예요. 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해 복습도 하고, 모르는 것은 교수님께 질문하기로 했어요. 장학금을 받으려면 좋은 성적이 필요하니까 이번 학기에는 더 꾸준히 공부해야 해요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo is taking a Korean class this semester. Because the presentation assignment must be finished before the midterm, Minseo made a schedule with a friend. Since the presentation counts toward the grade, they decided to start preparing from today. During exam period, Minseo will study at the library every day. In order to get a good grade on the final, Minseo will review and ask the professor about things they do not know. Since good grades are needed for a scholarship, Minseo has to study more consistently this semester.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 언제까지 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요?
시험 기간 동안 어디에서 공부할 거예요?

culturalNote.title: Grades Shape The Schedule
culturalNote.body: Korean school conversations often connect assignments, exams, grades, and future goals. A student may talk about 과제 and 발표 first, then 중간고사 or 기말고사, then 성적, 장학금, or 전공. The natural language is practical: 끝내야 해요, 준비하기 시작했어요, 시험 기간 동안, 합격하기 위해.
culturalNote.tip: Use 선생님 for school or language teachers, and 교수님 for university professors.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence gives a school obligation?
options: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요.
중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝낼 리가 없어요.
inlineExercises.correct: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence states a study decision?

inlineExercises.explanation: Put 동안 directly after the time span noun.

inlineExercises.prompt: 과제___ 해야 해요. (I have to do the assignment.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 하다 takes the assignment as an object, so 과제를 fits. 가 would make the assignment the subject.
-아/어야 해요 gives an obligation. 발표하다 becomes 발표해야 해요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'I decided to study at the library during exam period.' (Start with 시험 기간 동안.)
inlineExercises.correct: 시험 기간 동안 도서관에서 공부하기로 했어요
inlineExercises.explanation: 동안 gives the period, and 도서관에서 gives the study place. -기로 했어요 states the decision.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'I started studying for the midterm.'
inlineExercises.explanation: V-기 시작하다 means start doing. 준비하다 becomes 준비하기 before 시작했어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: '시험 동안에 합격하기 위해서 공부해요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 합격하다 takes the exam target with 에. 동안 is for a time span, not the exam you pass.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence states a personal study decision?
inlineExercises.explanation: -기로 했어요 marks a decision. -아/어야 해요 marks obligation instead.
N을 위해서 marks the goal or thing you are working for. 성적을 위해서 is natural for grade-related study.

bullets: Core flow: finish assignments before midterms, start preparing, study during exam period, and study for final goals.
V아/어야 해요 expresses school obligations; V기로 했어요 reports study decisions.
N 동안 marks a study period, while V기 위해서 marks a deliberate academic purpose.
과제, 발표, 중간고사, 기말고사, 성적, 장학금, 전공, and 교수님 should appear in real school sentences, not as isolated labels.

writingTask.prompt: Write a short note about your study plan: what you must do, what you decided, when you started, and why.
writingTask.hint: Use V-아/어야 해요 for obligation, V-기로 했어요 for a decision, V-기 시작하다 for starting, N 동안 for a period, V/A-(으)니까 for a reason, and V-기 위해서 for purpose.
writingTask.model: 다음 주에 중간고사가 있으니까 매일 도서관에서 공부해야 해요. 그래서 시험 기간 동안 친구하고 같이 공부하기로 했어요. 좋은 성적을 받기 위해서 지난주부터 공부하기 시작했어요.
writingTask.modelEn: Since there's a midterm next week, I have to study at the library every day. So I decided to study together with a friend during the exam period. To get good grades, I started studying last week.

canDo: Say what I have to do for school (과제를 내야 해요)
State a decision or study plan (같이 공부하기로 했어요)
Say when an action started (공부하기 시작했어요)
Give a reason that leads to a plan (시험이 있으니까 도서관에 가요)
State an academic purpose (장학금을 받기 위해서 공부해요)
